## Observation (from code, 2026-11-19 PST)
`highbred-fabled-lobo` (Gerrit 3452, fa383b1d195) stopped the Cloud ACLI transport from re-running `jira workitem create` after a non-zero exit, because the create may already have landed. The code review of that change named 2 sibling paths with the same shape; neither is changed there:
- Data Center: `_IssuesMixin.create_issue` (`src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py`) wraps the REST create in `_with_connection_retry`, which re-runs it on connection faults, including a fault after the request was sent.
- Cloud comments: `_NON_REPLAYABLE_COMMANDS` in `src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py` lists only `jira workitem create`, so `jira workitem comment create` is still retried after any non-zero exit and can post a duplicate comment.

Not established: whether either path has produced a duplicate in production. That needs a search of the Jira project for duplicate issues created seconds apart, and for repeated comments.

### Further observation (from code and library source, 2026-11-19 PST)
- The Data Center client is built by `build_client_from_settings` (`src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`) as `jira.JIRA(server=..., token_auth=..., options=...)` with no `max_retries`. In `jira` 3.8 (the `[jira-datacenter]` extra pins `jira>=3.8,<4`), `JIRA.__init__` defaults `max_retries=3` and sets it on its `ResilientSession`, whose `request` loop treats every `requests` `ConnectionError` as recoverable for any HTTP method, POST included, and also re-sends a 429 response. So a DC create or comment is re-sent inside the library (up to 4 sends) before rebar's own `_with_connection_retry` sees the fault, and rebar then re-runs the whole call up to 3 times. Changing only `_with_connection_retry` would leave the library replay in place.
- The DC comment add (`_CommentsMixin.add_comment`, `jira_datacenter/_links.py`) has the same shape as the DC create: a create-type write wrapped in `_with_connection_retry`.
- Both failure outcomes are recoverable without a replay: the create payload already carries the `rebar-id:<local_id>` label (added by `highbred-fabled-lobo`; DC passes it through `_translate_create_fields`), so the next pass's label lookup binds a landed issue; outbound comments are deduplicated on the next pass by decoded body equality (`src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_comments.py`), so a landed comment is not posted again.

## Approach
Extend the existing "no replay of a create" rule from `highbred-fabled-lobo` to the remaining create-type writes. No config key, env var or flag; the behaviour is unconditional.
1. Cloud comment create: add `("jira", "workitem", "comment", "create")` to `_NON_REPLAYABLE_COMMANDS` in `acli_subprocess.py`. `_run_acli` then raises on the first non-zero exit for it, except a detected 429, which Jira rejects without applying and which keeps its retry. This is the same mechanism and the same 429 carve-out the issue create uses.
2. Data Center: one retry layer, owned by rebar. `build_client_from_settings` passes `max_retries=0` to the `jira.JIRA` client so the library never re-sends a request; `_with_connection_retry` stays the single retry policy for every DC call. Reads keep their connection-fault retries (3 attempts, 2 s/5 s backoff) and their opted-in 429 `Retry-After` retry. What reads lose is the library's own extra layer: its retry of a 429 without a `Retry-After` header and of a 503 with one. That matches rebar's documented DC policy (`retry.py`: retry eligibility follows the header; only an opted-in 429 is retried), which the hidden library layer was overriding.
3. Data Center create-type writes: `_with_connection_retry` gains a keyword `replayable: bool = True`. With `replayable=False`, a connection fault is retried only when it shows the request never reached the server: a `requests` `ConnectTimeout`, or a `ConnectionError` whose cause is urllib3's connect-phase `ConnectTimeoutError`/`NewConnectionError` (connection refused, DNS failure). Any other connection fault (read timeout, reset, remote disconnect, builtin `TimeoutError`) is raised on the first attempt. `create_issue` and `add_comment` pass `replayable=False`. The TLS-error and HTTP-error branches are unchanged.
Not changed: DC and Cloud link create (`create_issue_link`, `jira workitem link create`), which link two existing issues rather than create a new record; issue updates, labels and transitions, which do not create anything.
Portability: no process, signal, path or encoding change.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py`: comment create added to `_NON_REPLAYABLE_COMMANDS`.
- `src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py`: `replayable` keyword and the never-sent classification.
- `src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`: `max_retries=0` on the client.
- `src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py`: `create_issue` passes `replayable=False`.
- `src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_links.py`: `add_comment` passes `replayable=False`.
- `tests/unit/reconciler/test_create_writes_not_replayed.py` (new).
- `tests/unit/reconciler/test_dc_pat_required.py`: its fake client constructor takes a fixed `(server, token_auth, options)` signature and must accept the new `max_retries` keyword.

## Testing
New `tests/unit/reconciler/test_create_writes_not_replayed.py`, written first and seen failing before the fix:
- Cloud comment: a fake ACLI records each `jira workitem comment create` to a state file and then exits non-zero; `add_comment` raises and the file holds exactly 1 record. A 429 on the first comment create is still retried and ends with 1 recorded comment.
- DC create and DC comment: a fake client records the call and then raises an ambiguous connection fault (builtin `TimeoutError`, and a `requests` `ConnectionError` read-phase fault when `requests` is importable); `create_issue`/`add_comment` raise and the fake records exactly 1 call.
- DC never-sent fault: a `requests` `ConnectTimeout` (or `ConnectionError` caused by `NewConnectionError`) on the first create is retried and ends with 1 recorded create.
- DC reads unchanged: `get_issue` still retries an ambiguous connection fault (3 attempts).
- Client construction: `build_client_from_settings` passes `max_retries=0` (spy on `_jira_client_class`).
- Existing `test_dc_rate_limit_retry.py`, `test_cloud_create_single_attempt.py` and `test_acli_auth_failure.py` stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each of the 2 paths either no longer replays a write that may have landed (verified by a regression test that fails the first attempt after the write is recorded and asserts one result), or is shown with evidence to be safe.
- [ ] The Data Center client no longer re-sends requests itself (`max_retries=0`), verified by a construction test.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/reconciler` passes and `make verify` passes.
